newsitem.title: GERMANY: Moody's cuts Siemens snr debt to Aa1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's cuts Siemens snr debt to Aa1.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday that it had downgraded the senior debt of Germany's Seimens AG to AA1 from AAA.

"The downgrade reflects Moody's expectation that the cost of building leading positions in selected market segments and Siemen's slow progress in its drive to improve the cost competitiveness of core businesses will cause the company's exceptional balance sheet strength and liquidity to deteriorate in the intermediate term," Moody's said in a statement.

Moody's added, however, that it had confirmed the Prime-1 rating for the short-term debt of Siemens and its guaranteed subsidiaries, as well as the VMIG-1 rating for the industrial revenue bonds of DeKalb and Fulton Counties of Georgia in the United States, backed by Siemens Energy and Automation.
The rating agency said it believed Siemens's gradual expansion into emerging markets would lead the company into "areas of fierce international competition and rising pressure on overall margins".

"The current programmes to raise productivity and reduce cost so far have proven insufficient to recoup the price declines apparent not only in these emerging, but also in the mature markets of the industrialised countries," it said.
Siemens, headquartered in Munich, is a diversified electrical and electronics company with sales of around $54 billion in the fiscal year ending September 30, 1996.
